extraction.name: CommonCatalog
extraction.description: A dataset of roughly 70 million open-licensed Creative-Commons (CC) images paired with high-quality synthetic captions generated via a transfer learning technique called telephoning.
extraction.creator: Aaron Gokaslan, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, Volodymyr Kuleshov
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced by starting with the YFCC100M dataset and re-scraping the high-resolution images from Flickr based on the IDs provided in the YFCC100M metadata, excluding images with non-derivative (ND) licenses.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Almost all CC images lack the captions necessary to train a high-quality T2I model. Those that do have associated text often just include the image title or a URL.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were center-cropped and resized to a maximum size of 512x512 pixels for the captioning process. At training time of the diffusion model, all images remain in their native resolution.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Captions were synthesized using a pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model, which takes the CC images as inputs and performs a 'lossy compression' to produce short-text synthetic captions. This transfer-learning process is referred to as telephoning.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The synthetic captions showed reduced diversity of n-grams compared to ground-truth captions, visualized through a decrease in unique trigrams. However, the CLIP Score for synthetic captions exceeded that of ground-truth captions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset provides an alternative method for navigating copyright concerns in generative AI by training only on open-licensed, Creative-Commons data with known provenance, avoiding the unclear provenance and copyright issues of massive web-scraped datasets like LAION-5B.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The model trained on this dataset underperformed in several categories, including faces, general photography, and paintings. The synthetic captions also exhibit reduced diversity of n-grams.
